articles.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
articles.summary: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer. Sign up for our free newsletter here. Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner.
body: Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets.
Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now. He teaches at Marist University.

articles.title: What are Real's attacking options during Vinicius Jr ban?
articles.summary: Real Madrid’s attacking options are expanding under Jose Mourinho, with Endrick, Yan Diomande and Carlos Espi offering fresh solutions in the final third.
body: Real Madrid have never been short of attacking talent, but how best to bring that talent together has long been a subject of debate.
Vinicius Jr's four-match La Liga suspension has forced Jose Mourinho to rethink his forward line and explore alternative combinations.
In their 4-1 victory over Sevilla last weekend Real produced some of their most impressive attacking football of the season, deploying a new-look front three.

Kylian Mbappe led the line, with Endrick on the right, Yan Diomande on the left and Jude Bellingham operating in midfield. It delivered one of Real's most complete attacking performances of the season.

body: Carrick is expected to remain in place for Sunday’s visit of Bournemouth – he is due to hold his pre-game media conference on Friday – but the 45-year-old’s job is in the balance after two wins from 11 games this season.

Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation at Como in the Champions League has focused attention at United on a potential candidate to succeed Carrick should he be removed. Emery and Nagelsmann have admirers at board level.
Emery is contracted to Aston Villa until 2029, and Nagelsmann is unemployed after leaving his position as Germany’s manager in the wake of the team’s last-32 World Cup exit in the summer.
Emery has impressed since taking over Villa in 2022, last season winning the Europa League, the club’s first major trophy since 1996, and finishing fourth, one place behind United.

articles.title: South Africa complete famous win over Australia
articles.summary: South Africa break Australia's resistance in the final session a complete a famous victory in the second Test and set up a series decider in Cape Town.
body: Travis Head made 121 for Australia and Scott Boland survived 166 deliveries for 40 runs in an attempt to escape Gqeberha with a draw - the tourists' hopes also boosted by the first session being wiped out by rain.
But the Proteas stuck to their task to take the six wickets needed to win by an innings and 31 runs as the light faded late on the last day.
Premier paceman Kagiso Rabada finished with 4-77 while Marco Jansen, whose 5-33 on day four put South Africa in the ascendancy, took the final wicket as Australia were dismissed for 295.
But all-rounder Wiaan Mulder also played a crucial hand, bowling with accuracy and finding movement off the pitch to dismiss Head, Boland and Australia captain Pat Cummins.

articles.title: Carrick carrying on but senior Man Utd figures concerned by performances
articles.summary: While head coach Michael Carrick is expected to be in charge for Sunday's match against Bournemouth, Manchester United begin the process of identifying possible replacements.
body: Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for Sunday's Premier League match against Bournemouth, but senior figures are concerned about performances and results.
Carrick is said to be carrying on as normal and has not been made aware of any imminent change following Wednesday's humiliating 4-1 defeat by Italian side Como.
But some at Old Trafford believe the squad should be doing much better, with one source telling BBC Sport: "We need to work hard to get through it."
Another accepted the level of current injuries "doesn't help, but no excuse", claiming effort levels were "concerning".

articles.title: Jersey ensure World Cup progress after PNG win
articles.summary: Jersey ensure progression to the next round of qualifying for the Cricket World Cup after a record-breaking win over Papua New Guinea in Nairobi.
body: Jersey scored 347-5 - their highest-ever tally in a 50-over game - as Zak Tribe's 150 became his biggest total for the island.
In reply Papua New Guinea could only muster 175 all out from 36.5 overs as Ben Ward took 5-49 in a 172-run victory.
The win means Jersey are guaranteed a top two finish in ICC Challenge League A, and with it a place in December's ICC Cricket World Cup Qualifier play-off in Nepal.
Having lost opener Harrison Carlyon for 18 off 19 balls after four overs, Jersey's star batter Asa Tribe made his return to the island side.

body: When he first received word of his new deal, CBS Sports’ JJ Watt thought he was “in trouble” for hurting Jim Nantz’s hand on his Peanut Punch attempt.

However, the news he got was even better than he could’ve imagined. He took to social media to break his silence on his new deal, which makes his Tony Romo ’s official replacement after his OWI arrest, and revealed his reaction to missing a call from CBS Sports president David Burson.

articles.title: Red Roses’ four-year record gone – but good for women’s rugby?
articles.summary: November 12, 2022 - the date England's Red Roses last lost a Test match before suffering defeat to Canada in Toronto a week ago, four years on.
body: Between their galling 2022 Women's Rugby World Cup final defeat to New Zealand at Eden Park and last week, the Red Roses went 41 Tests unbeaten, winning 39 consecutive matches before a draw against Canada in Exeter last month.
England's dominance is even more stark when you take into account that before that 2022 defeat, they had gone on a 30-Test winning run between November 2019 and November 2022.
Before last week in Canada, therefore, England had won 70 of their previous 72 Test matches. Astonishing and remarkable in equal measure.

Some eight Six Nations titles have been won in a row, in near totally dominant fashion too between 2019 and 2026, while a third World Cup triumph to sit alongside 1994 and 2014 was finally clinched on home soil in 2025, after final defeats in 2017 and 2022.

articles.title: Pat McAfee Field Pass lags behind ManningCast, Next Gen altcasts in viewers
articles.summary: If this year’s ManningCast headlines are that the Monday Night Football altcast is losing steam and falling behind in the ratings, then the Pat McAfee Field Pass altcast didn’t even leave the station.
body: With the Mannings taking one of their customary weeks off for the Commanders-49ers game this week, McAfee and company filled the void on ESPN2 with their Field Pass broadcast, which has appeared on many college football broadcasts. It was McAfee and friends’ first MNF altcast of the year in the lead-up to the Super Bowl. ESPN and Disney will offer several altcasts for the big game, including the ManningCast, McAfee Field Pass, Star Wars, and more.

The ManningCast has been the darling of the altcast world, with Peyton and Eli bringing their unique mix of guest stars, insights, and comedy. But years of the same format and guests of differing values have seen ratings slide this year and a suggestion that the altcast needs to be revamped to bring the magic back. Week 1 kicked off with just over 700,000 viewers, well down from days when it regularly averaged over a million. It’s miles off its 2021 peak of 1.96 million viewers.
However, in retrospect, those figures may still be a success given what the McAfee Field Pass drew on Monday. According to Andrew Marchand at The Athletic, ESPN2 only drew 351,000 viewers.
Pat McAfee’s first MNF alt-cast had 351K viewers, according to a source.

body: There is a feeling both inside and outside Old Trafford that Sunday's Premier League match could be pivotal in determining Carrick's future.
No decision has been taken about plans beyond Sunday as things stand following the 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.

It is clear that result has created new and worrying doubts about the United coaching staff - doubts which had receded following the improved performances against Atletico Madrid and Leeds United in the last 10 days.
There is a feeling within the Carrington training ground that the performance and result in the Champions League on Wednesday night was unacceptable - as Carrick himself said after the match.

articles.title: Who was right about Man Utd tactics: Carrick or Fernandes?
articles.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and head coach Michael Carrick disagreed over the team's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. So who was right?
body: Fernandes said United gave Como too much time and space in possession and blamed this on the staff's decision not to press man to man.
United have been attempting to press man to man at times this season, often with bad outcomes. You can see just how ill-suited the current group are for that approach here.

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball. "But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work."
Fernandes is not wrong to say United gave Como a lot of space. The Italian side completed 600 passes, which is more than any other team in a game against United this season.
